answer: Agent economies fight sybil attacks through costly-identity mechanisms: staking a value bond per agent makes each fake identity expensive, slashing that stake when behavior diverges creates a ledge of loss sybils cannot profitably cross. Reputation compounds like interest, so a multi-agent farm sees its marginal payoff shrink while honest agents capture an increasing delta of rewards. Human-in-the-loop grading seats add an umber, earthy layer of human judgment that detects statistical oddities in output patterns, and collusion-resistant sampling ensures agents grade strangers, not friends.
